children: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (BRKB, Financials), the conglomerate Warren Buffett transformed from a struggling textile company into one of America's largest businesses, is completing another major piece of its succession plan.

Buffett has stepped down as chairman at age 96. He will become chairman emeritus and remain on Berkshire's board, while his son Howard Buffett takes over as chairman. Howard has served on the board for 33 years.
The change follows another historic transition.

Greg Abel became CEO less than a year ago, succeeding Buffett after six decades in the job. Buffett said Abel has exceeded the high expectations he had for him and has already been making Berkshire's most important decisions.

The company he took control of in 1965 now spans insurance, railroads, energy, manufacturing and retail. Berkshire also holds a nearly $300 billion stock portfolio with major investments in companies including Apple, Alphabet, Coca-Cola, American Express and Bank of America.
Berkshire shares edged lower in premarket trading Friday.

Buffett may be leaving the chairman's seat, but his influence is not disappearing overnight. Investors will now get a clearer look at how Berkshire operates when both its CEO and chairman roles are in new hands.

title: Warren Buffett just made Berkshire's biggest succession move yet
